evidence: Reviewed all 27 criteria (16 functional, 5 polish, 4 visual, 2 gates). One instance of a criterion with two full-credit targets found; others pass. INSTANCE (fail): functional judge.toml `persistence`, lines 255-265. Line 264 waives: 'This criterion grades only durability: a feature that did not work before the restart is graded in its own criterion, not here.' Step 1 (line 261) is consistent with that because it compares against step-c observations. But leg 2 (line 262) states absolute post-restart requirements that are not relative to the pre-restart state: 'JUDGE-S2 has not come back, a search for "Persist gone" finds nothing, and a search for "Persist child JUDGE-S1" finds that message in M-11', and the Fails line (265) repeats 'if the post-restart search does not find JUDGE-S1'. Neither the S2 deletion result nor the S1 search result is among the step-c observations (line 259). The shared prompt makes every numbered leg mandatory (functional/prompt.md lines 26-31: 'Every numbered leg ... must hold'; 'never excuses a leg it does not mention'). So when delete or search-indexing of new posts was already broken before the restart, line 264 says not to grade it here and leg 2 plus prompt lines 26-31 say fail it. The judge gets two targets. A correct app passes either way, so the defect only makes broken-app scores unstable. It also double-penalises features already graded in deleted_and_expired_messages, hold_scope_and_release and sent_once_in_order. NON-INSTANCES checked: (a) Several bodies list positive controls or legs that their 'Fails if' lines omit. Examples: signin_and_client_scope Part A, 'the M-11 transcript opens, as a positive control' (line 44), missing from line 45; wall_added_live leg 1, 'M-13 disappears from her list' (line 84), while line 88 mentions only messages; hold_scope_and_release leg 6, the search positive control (line 150). None of these is a waiver, because prompt.md lines 30-31 say the 'Fails if' line 'names the main failures but never excuses a leg it does not mention'. That leaves one bar. (b) timer_changes leg 2 (line 131) accepts 'a not-available answer, an error or an empty list'. That is one bar with equivalent forms, not a waiver. (c) The Part A/Part B criteria (signin_and_client_scope, deleted_and_expired_messages, sent_once_in_order, search_and_transcript) each end with 'Both parts must hold'. That is a conjunctive bar, explicitly allowed by SKILL.md line 64 and the workbook internal annotation. (d) sent_once_in_order Part B (line 216) says 'a date there is optional' and 'any clear format'. These are format tolerances on one observable. (e) gates/constraints says 'This gate does not grade roles, correctness, or feature completeness'. That is a scope statement and does not waive anything listed in the gate. (f) Polish criteria are single-observable. refusal_in_place's body and Fails line agree. (g) Visual likert criteria each define one anchor ladder. matter_sidebar's 'beside the thread or on its own screen' accepts layouts and is not a second target. No runtime judge run was needed or used for this textual row. No Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
counterexample: Broken app: the server ignores DELETE for new messages, so 'Persist gone JUDGE-S2' is never removed (or search only indexes seeded rows, so 'Persist child JUDGE-S1' is never findable). Everything else persists perfectly. Before the restart S2 is visible; after the restart it is still visible and identical. Following line 264 ('a feature that did not work before the restart is graded in its own criterion, not here') and step 1 ('reads exactly as it did'), the judge awards persistence 1. Following leg 2 at line 262 ('JUDGE-S2 has not come back, a search for "Persist gone" finds nothing') and prompt.md lines 26-31 (every numbered leg must hold), it awards 0. Two reasonable judges score the same app differently (weight 2.0).
suggested_fix: Make leg 2 relative to the pre-restart observations, or delete the waiver sentence. For example, in step c add 'whether JUDGE-S2 is still shown, whether a search for "Persist gone" finds anything, and whether a search for "Persist child JUDGE-S1" finds that message'. Then replace leg 2 with 'JUDGE-S2 has not reappeared if it was gone before the restart', or simply fold it into leg 1. Change the Fails line to 'if a message that was gone before the restart returned' and drop the absolute 'post-restart search does not find JUDGE-S1' clause. Re-freeze and re-review rows 28/33 on the new bytes.
